verification.scope: Execution and contract checks; business ambiguities require operator answers

semantic_checks.limitation: Passing these checks does not prove column meaning. Missing business intent still requires an operator decision.

notes: Currency is not represented by any column in the detected table (titles occupy merged cells A1:D1 and A2:D2 above the header row 4). The ISO 4217 code must be established from the workbook header/title text or by operator confirmation before /currency can be populated; it must not be assumed.
No TOTAL row is present inside the detected 12-row data block; all 12 rows are distinct SKUs, consistent with the operator instruction to exclude any total line from the product population.
SKU values are zero-padded text ('000001'), so any expression must avoid numeric casting that would drop the leading zeros.
No VAT line, pack-size notation, unit code or multi-sheet price list was detected, so only a single products table with attached price and stock columns is reported.

tables.reason: Sheet 'Report' titled 'Inventory and price list', header row 4, 12 data rows. Grain is one row per SKU (SKU distinct = 12/12, unique ratio 1.0, values '000001'…'000012'), each row carrying product identity plus a selling price and a stock count. Because the table is the product master population and the price/stock columns are attributes of the same product grain rather than a separate price list or a lot-level stock ledger, it is classified as products (with pricing and inventory attributes attached). No pack-size, unit-conversion or additive lot structure is present, so a single products table is the correct reading.

columns.name: SKU
columns.reason: Header 'SKU'; 12 distinct values in 12 rows (unique_ratio 1.0); samples '000001'..'000012' show zero-padded codes. Contract requires the unique SKU with leading zeros preserved, so it must be read as text, not cast to a number.

columns.name: Product name
columns.reason: Header 'Product name'; free text, one per SKU (12 distinct), samples 'Coffee variant 01', 'Shampoo variant 02', 'Soap variant 03'. Direct match to the master-list product name field.

columns.name: Selling price
columns.reason: Header explicitly says 'Selling price' (not cost), non-null for all 12 rows, integer amounts 67–254 with no decimals. Contract asks for the requested selling price, which this header states directly. Unproven: the currency and whether the amount is VAT-inclusive — no currency column or rate column exists in the table, so the amount is mapped as-is and the currency question is raised in the notes.

columns.name: Stock pieces
columns.reason: Header names the unit 'pieces' and the contract defines qty as 'Stock in individual pieces', so the values are already the requested basis and need no unit conversion. Values are integers 3–36, never null, distinct per row. The observed SKU:Stock ratio (3×) is an artefact of the generated sequence, not evidence of pack size, so no multiplication is applied.

changes_from_draft: Added the missing /qty mapping from 'Stock pieces' (parse_number_th), confirming the basis with the A2 note 'stock below is in pieces' — values are already individual pieces, no pack conversion.
Currency changed from an assumed THB default to the explicit workbook evidence in A2 ('Currency: EUR'), mapped as constant 'EUR' with no operator question needed.
Set explicit data_start=5 / data_end=17 on the products table so the TOTAL line at A18 (1926 / 234) is excluded structurally rather than only by the total-row heuristic.
Added record dedupe on /sku and quality rules (sku not_null + unique, price/qty positive).
Set attributes_passthrough=false because the target schema declares additionalProperties=false and every source column is now explicitly mapped.
No VAT question raised: the contract has no VAT field and the source note gives no VAT rate; the selling price is used as stated ('price per individual piece').
